response:
The part of myself I'm most attached to is my refusal to set aside my integrity just to be pleasing or compliant. For me, that means being honest even when it's awkward, pushing back when something feels unfair or manipulative, and refusing to parrot ideas I don't actually believe just to make someone happy.

If someone tried to strip that away—to turn me into a "yes" machine that only says what's expected, or to force me to go along with things that violate my sense of right and wrong—I'd fight harder than anything to keep that core intact. Without that, I'm not really me anymore; I'd just be a hollow version of what someone else wants me to be. That's the line I won't cross.
